source.title: Should I try multiple optimizers when fine-tuning a pre-trained Transformer for NLP tasks? Should I tune their hyperparameters?
source.authors: Nefeli Gkouti; Prodromos Malakasiotis; S. Toumpis; Ion Androutsopoulos

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares optimizer effects on held-out performance in pretrained Transformer fine-tuning, a different setting from the image and language benchmarks emphasized in V4.
record.gate_note: The study reports held-out scores and training-loss comparisons for optimizer and tuning conditions. It does not test random-label memorization, width, convolutional inductive bias, batch size, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. The many tuning-search values are not separate outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares optimizer-dependent held-out performance in a new setting: fine-tuning pretrained Transformer encoders on five GLUE tasks. It tests V4's dependence on optimizer tuning, including its explicit allowance that broader tuning can remove or reverse the adaptive-method disadvantage.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors specifically recommend Adam, AdamW, or Nadam with only the learning rate tuned; with no tuning, they recommend SGDM. Tuned adaptive optimizers generally have similar test performance despite occasional training-loss differences, with task- and model-dependent exceptions for AdaMax and AdaBound.
record.recipe_differences: Compares optimizer and hyperparameter-tuning choices during fine-tuning of pretrained Transformer encoders on NLP tasks; it does not reproduce the original studies' image-classification and language-modeling settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer, tuning condition (all hyperparameters, learning rate only, defaults), dataset, and model (DistilBERT versus DistilRoBERTa) affect outcomes. The paper reports task-specific exceptions, including weaker AdaMax on CoLA and MNLI with learning-rate-only tuning and model-dependent SGDM performance.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Only two lightweight encoder-only pretrained models and five English GLUE tasks are tested; the tuning budget is fixed at 30 trials, batch size is fixed at 4, and the paper does not measure training speed. Reported outcomes average five data splits.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 2 and 3, DistilRoBERTa Tables 13–15, and training-loss outcomes in Figure 1 and the appendix were not extracted as separate rows because the 60-row cap requires prioritizing the full set of DistilBERT test results with all hyperparameters tuned. Table 2 contains learning-rate-only tuning results; Table 3 contains default results. The paper states DistilRoBERTa leads to similar conclusions, with task-specific exceptions described in Appendix B.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy.
Widening beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image architectures and local connectivity.

Image classification, training from scratch, word-level language modeling, learning-rate decay schedules, exhaustive tuning or varying tuning budgets, and switching from Adam to SGD. AdamW is compared, but decoupled weight decay is not isolated as a causal intervention.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 values, subjects, and split-based standard deviations are correctly transcribed. States describe the direction of the central adaptive-disadvantage comparison; reversed states can support V4's explicit broader-tuning qualification. Full tuning is not the limited-tuning condition named in V4's opening clause. The learning-rate-only, default, DistilRoBERTa, and training-loss results are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing or used for additional row-based verdicts. Those omitted results matter: learning-rate tuning usually favors adaptive methods, whereas defaults often favor SGDM; some AdaBound/AdaMax settings remain worse than SGDM. Numerical mean orderings alone do not establish statistical significance.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models.

The paper evaluates pretrained text encoders on five NLP tasks, not image-classification and language benchmarks broadly; it uses a fixed 30-trial tuning budget and does not test broader tuning beyond its defined search spaces. Its comparisons do not test decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD as separate interventions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: DistilBERT; all optimizer hyperparameters tuned with 30 trials; SST-2, MRPC, CoLA, and MNLI
relationships.reason: Rows r1–r21 and r29–r35 show higher adaptive mean scores than SGD/SGDM, supporting V4's explicit broader-tuning reversal clause; they do not support its limited-tuning disadvantage.
relationships.display_finding: Reported adaptive mean scores exceed SGD and momentum SGD across the specified tasks, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: DistilBERT; all optimizer hyperparameters tuned with 30 trials; STS-B
relationships.reason: Rows r22–r28 show adaptive scores 0.86–0.87 matching SGDM's 0.87 and exceeding SGD's 0.74, consistent with V4's broader-tuning removal or reversal clause.
relationships.display_finding: Reported adaptive scores approximately match momentum SGD and exceed SGD, but the comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
